description: Hibernia's lore, myths and places as its people tell them, from Living Server, rewritten.

lines.text: Funny how the azure hate the glimmers more than they hate us.
The azure preach at the glimmers all day and the glimmers just keep glowing. Patience of a saint.
They say Cuuldurach is the only male dragon of the three. The Norse argue about theirs.
People say the dragon drops nothing but coin. Those people have never been on a raid.
I think Evern is older than the frontier keeps. The stones were there first and the keeps went up around them.
Heard the Marfach Caverns serve some power that wants all three realms on its knees. Cheerful neighbours.
Dare: walk into Evern's stone ring, touch one stone and run. Nobody has taken me up yet.
Counted the stones around Evern once. Got twenty three, a friend got twenty two. The fairies moved one.
Never cut a thorn tree in Hibernia. The folk under the hills remember.
I bet even the faerie court steps around Juggernaut when he comes through.
The Siabra are Elf kin gone wrong, and they hold more of Hibernia than people like to admit.
The old songs say we warred with the folk under the hills before we made peace against the Norse and the Britons.
The Firbolg say they were here when the hills were young. The Tuatha just smile at that.
The Siabra wayguards watch the roads like they still own the land. Maybe they do.
The dullahan rides when someone is about to die. Hear hooves and see no horse, run.
Heard a banshee wail right before a pull once. We wiped, of course. I do not pull after a wail now.
My grandmother said the door to the Otherworld opens only when the mist comes up from the bog.
The Bards say a horn hangs inside the Fianna's hill. Blow it three times and they wake.
My guild's old saying: the Otherworld is never far, it is just one step sideways.
The old maps leave the sea past the cliffs blank. I think the map maker just gave up.
Olcasgean is a child of Gaea, older than the Tuatha, and he has been sulking at the edge of the world ever since.
The Sylvan are trees that walk and talk and ask us for help. Still getting used to that.
Heard of a raid of fifty that fought Myrddraxis for an hour and came out with nothing but repair bills.
Myrddraxis is supposed to drop a scale that never breaks. Never seen one myself.
The Dagda's cauldron never runs empty in the old tales. That explains our soldiers.
They say there were meant to be more than six relics. I think one is hidden in Hibernia.
My old guild swore Nuada's sword was meant to be our third relic and just never turned up.
People say Bards are overpowered. We mez and run fast. That is called being useful.
Every realm thinks our Bards are overpowered. They are not wrong, and we are not giving them up.
A Bard with speed, mez and a heal is three classes in one kilt. Overpowered, and I love it.
Veterans told us the realm was bigger than the map. Turned out they were right.
The first time I saw a Sylvan move I swung at it. It was very polite about it.
The Firbolg were here first, and they remember things the rest of us never knew.
The Siabra hold more of this realm than the maps admit.
Every glen in Hibernia has a story, I have found maybe half of them.
Swam out past the coast once, the water just kept going. Turned back before it got too dark.
Dare: walk into the green door in Connacht if you find it. I will follow you.
